tips: Keep your armpits facing forward to lock the bar in place.
Keep the bar over mid-foot with a more upright torso than a back squat.
Work on shoulder and ankle mobility before adding load.

pause-pull-up.description: A pull-up variation that adds a brief isometric hold at the top of the movement, with the chin over the bar, before lowering back down.
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, arms fully extended.
Pull yourself up until your chin clears the bar.
Pause and hold that top position for a moment.
Lower yourself back down under control to a full hang.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: The pause removes momentum, so the pull is harder than a regular pull-up -- expect fewer reps.
Keep your shoulders engaged during the hold instead of relaxing into the bar.
Lower slowly instead of dropping straight into the next rep.

paused-ohp.description: An overhead press variation that pauses the bar at the shoulders, removing momentum to build strict pressing strength and overhead stability.
instructions: Set up with a barbell racked at shoulder height, feet shoulder-width apart, and the core braced.
Press the bar straight overhead until the elbows are fully locked out.
Lower the bar under control back down to the front of the shoulders.
Hold a full one-second pause at the shoulders, keeping tension and eliminating any bounce.
Press back up from the dead stop without using leg drive.
tips: Keep the pause strict -- no rebounding the bar off the shoulders.
Brace hard and keep the bar path vertical over the mid-foot.
Use a weight you can control through the dead-stop start.

pike-push-ups.description: A push-up performed with hips high in a pike position, pressing at a steep angle to load the shoulders.
instructions: Start in a downward dog position with hips high and hands shoulder-width apart.
Walk your feet closer to your hands.
Bend your elbows and lower your head toward the floor.
Keep your hips high throughout.
Press back up until your arms are fully extended.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: The higher your hips, the more the shoulders work.
Lower your head toward a spot slightly ahead of your hands.
Walk your feet closer to your hands to progress toward handstand push-ups.

pilates-roll-down.description: A standing articulation of the spine: the head leads a vertebra-by-vertebra roll towards the floor and back up, mobilising the whole back while the legs stay steady.
instructions: Stand tall with the feet hip-width apart and the arms hanging at the sides.
Drop the chin to the chest and start rolling down one vertebra at a time.
Let the arms and head hang heavy once the spine is fully rolled down.
Roll back up the same way, stacking the vertebrae one by one, head last.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep the knees soft so the movement comes from the spine, not the hamstrings.
Move slowly enough to feel each segment; speed defeats the purpose.
Keep the weight in the middle of the feet as you roll down.

pilates-spine-stretch-forward.description: A seated articulation: sitting tall with the legs apart, the spine curls forward segment by segment over the legs and then restacks vertebra by vertebra.
instructions: Sit tall with the legs straight and slightly wider than the hips, feet flexed.
Reach the arms forward at shoulder height.
Drop the chin and curl the spine forward one vertebra at a time, reaching past the toes.
Restack the spine from the base upwards until you are sitting tall again.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep the pelvis upright: the curl comes from the spine, not from tipping the hips.
Press the heels away throughout so the legs stay active.
Sit on a folded blanket if sitting upright already rounds the lower back.

planche-lean-floor.description: A floor progression toward the planche: from a high plank position, you lean your shoulders forward past your hands and hold, so that more of your bodyweight loads the shoulders and chest. It builds the straight-arm strength needed for the full planche.
instructions: Start in a high plank with your hands on the floor, a little below your hips and turned out slightly.
Lock your elbows and protract your shoulder blades so your upper back is slightly rounded and strong.
Lean your body forward until your shoulders are well in front of your hands.
Keep your whole body in a straight line, with your glutes squeezed and your core braced.
Hold the lean for the planned time while breathing steadily.
Shift back to the neutral plank to finish.
tips: Keep your arms straight; bending the elbows turns the hold into a push-up.
Push the floor away so your shoulder blades stay wide rather than sinking between the shoulders.
Lean only as far as you can keep the hold for several seconds; increase the lean gradually over weeks.

plate-loaded-glute-drive.description: A machine hip thrust performed on a plate-loaded glute drive, where the built-in back pad and foot platform set the position so the hips can extend against the load without setting up a bench.
instructions: Load the plate horns evenly and sit into the machine with your upper back against the pad and your feet flat on the platform.
Pull the hip pad or lap bar across your hips and adjust it so it sits on the crease of the hips, not on your stomach.
Set your feet so that your shins will be roughly vertical when your hips are at the top, and take hold of the handles.
Drive your hips up by squeezing the glutes until your thighs are level with your torso, and hold briefly at the top.
Lower under control until your hips are just short of the bottom of the range, and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Get the pad on the hip crease. Sitting it up on the stomach is the only genuinely uncomfortable thing this machine does, and it is fixed by moving the pad, not by adding padding.
Finish with the hips, not the lower back. If the ribs flare at the top you have run out of hip extension and started arching, which is where the machine stops training the glutes.
This is the hip thrust to reach for when the bench and barbell are taken -- the back pad and platform are part of the frame, so there is no setup to get wrong.

plate-pinch.description: A grip-training staple: pinch a weight plate by its rim and hold it for time, loading the thumb and finger flexors in sustained isometric work.
instructions: Stand a weight plate on its edge on the floor.
Squat down and pinch the plate by its rim between the fingers and thumb of one hand — no handles, just pinch.
Stand up and hold the plate at the side for time, keeping the arm straight.
Set it back down under control.
Repeat on the other hand.
tips: Start with a 5 kg / 10 lb plate and build up; pinching two plates together smooth-side out is a harder variation.
Chalk on the hands makes a huge difference; sweaty pinches fail fast.

plyo-push-up.description: An explosive push-up where the hands leave the floor at the top, training upper-body power.
instructions: Set up in a standard push-up position with hands shoulder-width.
Lower yourself with control until the chest nearly touches the floor.
Drive up explosively so the hands leave the floor.
Land softly with the elbows slightly bent.
Repeat without pausing for the prescribed reps.
tips: Keep the body in a straight line — no piking or sagging.
Land softly with bent elbows to absorb impact.
Drop to knees if you cannot clear the floor cleanly.

pull-up.description: A bodyweight compound pull targeting the lats and biceps.
instructions: Hang from a bar with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Pull yourself up until your chin is over the bar.
Lower yourself under control to a dead hang.
Repeat.
tips: Avoid swinging or kipping.
Engage your lats by pulling your elbows down.

push-up.description: A fundamental bodyweight exercise for the chest, shoulders, and triceps.
instructions: Start in a high plank position with hands shoulder-width apart.
Lower your body until your chest nearly touches the floor.
Push back up to the starting position.
Keep your body in a straight line throughout.
Repeat.
tips: Tuck your elbows toward your body rather than flaring them out wide.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes to prevent sagging hips.
Keep your neck neutral by gazing slightly ahead of your hands.

reclined-butterfly.description: A restful version of the butterfly stretch: lying back with the soles of your feet together and your knees dropped out to the sides, you open the inner thighs and hips under gravity. Resting your back and arms on the floor lets the legs relax into the stretch.
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and the soles of your feet flat on the floor.
Bring the soles of your feet together and let both knees fall out to the sides.
Rest your arms on the floor with your palms up, or place your hands on your belly.
Keep your lower back resting on the floor and your shoulders relaxed.
Breathe slowly and let your knees sink toward the floor for the planned time.
Bring your knees together with your hands to finish.
tips: Do not push the knees down with your hands; let gravity do the work so the inner thighs relax.
Slide your feet further from the hips to ease the stretch, or closer to deepen it.
Put a pillow or folded blanket under each knee if the stretch feels too strong.

reverse-grip-bent-over-row.description: A barbell row performed with an underhand grip, shifting emphasis toward the lower lats and biceps.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and grip a barbell underhand.
Hinge forward at the hips with a slight knee bend.
Let the bar hang with your arms extended.
Pull the bar to your lower abdomen by driving your elbows back.
Squeeze your back at the top.
Lower the bar with control.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Keep your back flat and your core braced throughout.
Maintain a fixed torso angle instead of heaving upright as you pull.
Keep the bar close to your legs throughout the movement.

reverse-plank.description: An isometric hold with the body facing upward, training the glutes, spinal erectors, and shoulder stability.
instructions: Sit on the floor with your legs extended in front of you.
Place your hands behind you with fingers pointing toward your feet.
Lift your hips off the floor to form a straight line from head to heels.
Squeeze your glutes and brace your core.
Hold the position for the desired duration.
Lower your hips with control to exit.
tips: Don't let your hips sag as the hold progresses.
Keep your gaze up to maintain a neutral neck.
Press evenly through your palms to reduce wrist strain.

revolved-chair-pose.description: Chair pose with a closed twist: the hips stay level and low while the chest rotates and one elbow hooks outside the opposite thigh.
instructions: Set up in chair pose with the knees bent, the hips back and the palms together at the chest.
Keep the knees level with each other so the hips do not open into the twist.
Rotate the chest to one side and hook the opposite elbow outside that thigh.
Press the palms together and hold for the prescribed time, lengthening the spine on each inhale.
Come back to centre and repeat on the other side.
tips: Line the knees up before you twist; a knee sliding forward fakes most of the rotation.
Rotate from the mid-back rather than pulling with the arm against the leg.
Keep the weight in the heels so the position stays a squat, not a lean.

ring-face-pull.description: A face pull using gymnastic rings for adjustable resistance and improved shoulder health.
instructions: Grip the rings and lean back so your body is at an angle.
Pull the rings toward your face, flaring elbows to the sides.
Hold briefly, then return.
Repeat.
tips: Adjust your body angle to control difficulty.
Externally rotate your arms at the top.

ring-push-up.description: A push-up performed on gymnastic rings, increasing the demand on stabilizers in the chest, shoulders, and core.
instructions: Set the rings just above floor height.
Grip the rings and assume a plank position with arms straight.
Lower the chest toward the rings, keeping the elbows close to the body.
Press back up to full arm extension.
Repeat for the prescribed reps.
tips: Keep the rings turned out at the top to engage the chest.
Brace the core — the rings will magnify any wobble.
Drop to knees to scale the difficulty.

romanian-deadlift.description: A hip-hinge movement emphasizing the hamstrings and glutes.
instructions: Stand holding a barbell at hip level with an overhand grip.
Hinge at the hips, pushing them back while keeping legs nearly straight.
Lower the bar along your legs until you feel a hamstring stretch.
Drive your hips forward to return to standing.
Repeat.
tips: Keep your spine neutral and avoid rounding the lower back.
Maintain the same slight knee bend for the entire rep.
Go only as deep as your hamstring flexibility allows.

russian-twist.description: A rotational core exercise targeting the obliques.
instructions: Sit on the floor with knees bent, lean back slightly.
Hold your hands together or hold a weight at chest level.
Rotate your torso to one side, then the other.
Keep your core braced throughout.
Repeat.
tips: Rotate from the torso rather than just swinging the arms.
Keep your chest lifted and your spine long as you twist.
Move at a controlled tempo instead of racing through reps.

scissor-kicks.description: A core exercise performed lying on the back, alternating straight-leg crosses to target the lower abdominals and hip flexors.
instructions: Lie flat on your back with your hands under your glutes.
Lift both legs a few inches off the floor.
Alternate crossing one leg over the other in a scissor motion.
Keep your lower back pressed into the floor.
Maintain a steady rhythm throughout.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Press your lower back into the floor throughout.
Keep your legs straight and close to the ground.
Move with control rather than speed.

seated-db-press.description: A seated pressing movement for the shoulders using dumbbells.
instructions: Sit on a bench with back support, holding dumbbells at shoulder height.
Press the dumbbells overhead until arms are fully extended.
Lower the dumbbells back to shoulder level.
Repeat.
tips: Keep your lower back against the pad instead of arching excessively.
Avoid clanging the dumbbells together at the top.
Keep your forearms vertical under the dumbbells throughout the press.

seated-dumbbell-tricep-extension.description: A seated overhead extension lowering a dumbbell behind the head, stretching and working the triceps.
instructions: Sit on a bench with a dumbbell held overhead in both hands.
Keep your upper arms vertical next to your ears.
Lower the dumbbell behind your head by bending your elbows.
Extend your arms to press the dumbbell back overhead.
Squeeze your triceps at the top.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Keep your upper arms vertical next to your ears.
Move only your forearms, keeping the elbows still.
Brace your core to avoid arching your lower back.

seated-spinal-twist.description: A seated rotation that stretches the obliques, mid-back and glutes by twisting toward a bent knee.
instructions: Sit with one leg straight and cross the other foot over it.
Brace the opposite elbow against the outside of the bent knee.
Rotate your torso toward the bent knee and look over your shoulder.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Switch sides and repeat.
tips: Sit tall and lengthen your spine before twisting.
Twist from the mid-back, not the lower back.

side-lunge.description: A lateral lunge stepping wide to one side, training the quads, glutes, and inner thighs through a side-to-side pattern.
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart and hands at your chest.
Step one leg wide to the side, keeping the other leg straight.
Bend the stepping knee and push your hips back into a lateral squat.
Keep your chest up and the working heel planted.
Drive through the bent leg to return to standing.
Complete reps on one side, then switch.
tips: Push your hips back as you bend the stepping knee.
Keep your trailing leg straight and both heels planted.
Keep your chest up rather than rounding forward.

side-lying-hip-adduction-hold.description: The top of the side-lying inner-thigh raise held for time: lying on one side with the top leg crossed over and the bottom leg lifted off the floor by the adductors.
instructions: Lie on one side with the bottom leg straight and the top leg crossed over it, foot flat on the floor.
Support the head on the lower arm and keep the hips stacked vertically.
Lift the bottom leg as high as it will go with the knee straight and the toes pointing forward.
Hold that lifted position for the prescribed time without rolling the hips back.
Lower the leg under control and repeat on the other side.
tips: The range is short; a few centimetres of lift with a still pelvis beats a big swing.
Keep the lifted leg in line with the torso rather than drifting forward.
Press the top foot lightly into the floor if you need to steady the position.

side-plank-leg-lift-hold.description: A side plank held with the top leg raised: the hips stay lifted and square while the top leg is abducted, adding a glute medius demand to the lateral trunk hold.
instructions: Set up in a side plank on the forearm with the elbow under the shoulder and the feet stacked.
Lift the hips until the body forms a straight line from the ankles to the head.
Raise the top leg to roughly hip height, keeping the toes pointing forward.
Hold the position for the prescribed time, keeping the hips high and the supporting shoulder stacked over the elbow.
Lower the leg and the hips under control and repeat on the other side.
tips: Push the supporting shoulder away from the ear so the chest does not collapse towards the floor.
Stop the set when the hips start to drop, not when the leg gets tired.
Bend the bottom knee to the floor for an easier version that keeps the leg lift intact.

single-arm-dumbbell-overhead-tricep-exte.description: A one-arm overhead tricep extension giving a long, unilateral stretch of the long head and training anti-side-bend core stability.
instructions: Stand or sit holding a dumbbell in one hand overhead, arm fully extended.
The palm faces forward; the other hand can hold your waist or an upright for stability.
Bend the elbow to lower the dumbbell behind the head in a controlled arc.
Keep the upper arm vertical and close to the head throughout.
Extend the elbow to return the dumbbell overhead.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch.
tips: Only the forearm moves — the upper arm stays glued in place.
Don't let the torso lean to the side; this is also a core exercise.

single-arm-plate-loaded-lateral-raise.description: The plate-loaded machine lateral raise worked one arm at a time, so each side lifts its own load and the two can be trained to the same standard.
instructions: Set the seat height so the pad pivot lines up with your shoulder, and load only the side you are about to work.
Sit with your back flat against the pad and place the outside of your working upper arm against its pad.
Hold the handle on the free side or rest that hand in your lap, and keep your torso square to the seat.
Push the working arm out and up against the pad until the upper arm is level with your shoulder, then lower it under control.
Complete all the repetitions on that side, then load and work the other side.
tips: Match the sides on the weaker arm, not the stronger one. Working one side at a time only tells you about an imbalance if you let the weaker side set the number.
Do not let the torso tip toward the working side. With load on one arm only, the machine no longer balances itself and leaning turns the raise into a side bend.
Start with the weaker arm so it sets the target, and give both sides the same rest.

single-leg-calf-raise.description: A unilateral calf raise that loads one calf at a time, exposing strength imbalances side to side.
instructions: Stand on one foot on the floor and lift the other foot off the ground, knee bent.
Keep the arms relaxed at your sides and brace your core to hold your balance.
Drive up onto the ball of the foot as high as possible.
Lower the heel back to the floor under control.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch.
tips: Pause at the top to maximize the contraction.
Lower slowly instead of dropping onto the heel.
Hold a dumbbell on the working side once bodyweight is too easy.

single-leg-hip-thrust.description: A hip thrust done on one leg: with your upper back resting on a flat bench and one foot planted on the floor, you drive your hips up until your body is level, holding the other knee raised. Working one side at a time isolates the glute and shows up any difference between the legs.
instructions: Sit on the floor with your back to a flat bench and rest your upper back against its edge, just below your shoulder blades.
Plant both feet flat on the floor with your knees bent, then lift one knee toward your chest and keep it there.
Keep your chin tucked toward your chest and your arms resting along the bench.
Drive through the heel of the planted foot and push your hips up until your body is level from your shoulders to your knee.
Squeeze your glute at the top without arching your lower back, then lower your hips under control.
Complete the planned repetitions, then switch legs.
tips: Keep the planted shin close to vertical at the top so the glute, rather than the hamstring, does most of the work.
Do not let your hips twist toward the lifted leg; keep your pelvis level throughout.
Anchor the bench against a wall so it cannot slide, and start with the two-leg hip thrust until the movement is smooth.

single-leg-rdl-hold.description: A balance hold at the bottom of a single-leg Romanian deadlift: standing on one leg, the torso is hinged forward and the other leg extends back in line with the body. It trains the hamstrings, glutes and trunk while challenging balance.
instructions: Stand on one leg with a slight bend in the knee and the arms hanging in front of you.
Hinge at the hip, sending the free leg straight back as the torso tips forward.
Keep the back flat and the hips square to the floor.
Stop when the torso and the free leg are roughly parallel to the floor and hold the position.
Return to standing under control, then switch legs.
tips: Think of a seesaw: the torso and the free leg move together.
Keep the hips level; do not let the free hip rotate upward.
Fix your gaze on a point on the floor ahead to help your balance.

ski-erg.description: A standing cardio exercise on a ski ergometer that combines a forceful double-pole pull with a small hip hinge to train full-body power and endurance.
instructions: Stand facing the SkiErg with the handles overhead and the feet about hip-width apart.
Brace the trunk and drive the handles down by pulling with the lats while hinging slightly at the hips.
Finish with the hands beside the thighs and the knees softly bent.
Let the cords retract as you return the arms overhead and stand tall.
Repeat smoothly while keeping the heels planted and the torso controlled.
tips: Lead the pull with the lats instead of turning it into an arm-only movement.
Keep the hinge compact; do not collapse into a deep squat.
Allow the handles to return under control so the cords stay taut.

smith-machine-bench-press.description: A bench press variation in the Smith machine, where the guided bar path adds stability for the chest.
instructions: Lie on a flat bench set inside a Smith machine.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width and unrack it.
Lower the bar under control to your mid-chest.
Pause briefly without bouncing.
Press the bar back up until your arms are fully extended.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Align the bench so the bar lands at mid-chest, not the neck.
Keep your shoulder blades pulled back and down against the bench.
Keep your feet planted and your glutes on the bench.

smith-machine-decline-bench-press.description: A bench press on a decline bench under the Smith machine, where the head-down angle and the guided bar path put the work on the lower chest.
instructions: Set a decline bench in the machine so the bar lines up with your lower chest when you lie down, and hook your legs under the pads.
Lie back with your head at the low end, take an overhand grip slightly wider than your shoulders and unrack the bar.
Lower the bar under control until it touches your lower chest, keeping your elbows at roughly forty-five degrees from your torso.
Press the bar back up until your arms are extended, without locking the elbows out hard.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then rack the bar before releasing your legs.
tips: Line the bench up before you load it. The bar only moves in one plane, so if the bench is a few centimetres out the bar will meet your throat or your stomach instead of your lower chest.
Secure your legs under the pads first. Head-down and unsecured, you slide toward the low end of the bench on the first hard rep.
Come down and sit up slowly between sets. Long sets with the head below the heart make people light-headed, and this variation is where it happens.

smith-machine-incline-bench-press.description: An incline press in the Smith machine, guiding the bar to target the upper chest and front delts.
instructions: Set an incline bench at 30-45 degrees inside a Smith machine.
Lie back and grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Unrack and lower the bar to your upper chest.
Pause briefly at the bottom.
Press the bar back up until your arms are extended.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Position the bench so the bar lands on the upper chest, not the throat.
Stack your wrists directly above your elbows.
Avoid driving your head forward off the bench as you press.

smith-machine-shoulder-press.description: A standing overhead press in the Smith machine, with the guided bar path providing stability for the shoulders.
instructions: Stand inside a Smith machine with your feet hip-width apart and the bar at shoulder level.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width at shoulder level.
Unrack the bar and press it overhead until your arms are extended.
Lower the bar back to shoulder level under control.
Keep your core tight throughout.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Stand directly under the bar path before unracking.
Tilt your head back slightly as the bar passes your face.
Avoid flaring your ribs as the bar travels overhead.

smith-machine-upright-row.description: An upright row on the Smith machine, pulling the guided bar up the front of the torso with the elbows leading, to work the side deltoids and the upper traps.
instructions: Set the bar at hip height, take an overhand grip a little wider than shoulder-width and stand close to it with your arms straight.
Unrack the bar and stand tall with your shoulders back and your core braced.
Pull the bar straight up the front of your body, leading with your elbows and keeping the bar close.
Stop when the bar reaches your lower chest and your elbows are level with your shoulders, then pause briefly.
Lower the bar under control until your arms are straight again, and repeat for the desired reps.
tips: Stop at chest height. Pulling the bar to the collarbone rotates the shoulder into the position that causes the impingement this exercise is known for.
Lead with the elbows, not the hands. If the wrists come up first the biceps take over and the side deltoids barely work.
Widen the grip if the movement pinches. A narrow grip forces more internal rotation, and the fixed bar path gives you nowhere else to go.

spiderman-push-up.description: A push-up in which one knee is drawn up toward the elbow on the same side as the body lowers, like a spider climbing a wall. It trains the chest, shoulders and triceps while the obliques and hip flexors hold the trunk steady.
instructions: Start in a high plank with the hands slightly wider than the shoulders and the body in a straight line.
Begin to lower the chest toward the floor and at the same time lift one foot off the floor.
Draw that knee out and up toward the elbow on the same side, keeping the hips low.
Press back up to the plank while returning the leg to the starting position.
Repeat on the other side and keep alternating.
tips: Keep the hips level; letting them pike or sag takes the work off the trunk.
Bring the knee toward the elbow without letting the foot touch the floor.
Lower with control and keep the elbows at about 45 degrees to the body.

squat.description: A compound lower-body movement targeting the quadriceps, glutes, and hamstrings.
instructions: Position the bar on your upper traps.
Unrack and step back, feet shoulder-width apart.
Brace your core and squat down until thighs are parallel.
Drive through your heels to stand back up.
Repeat.
tips: Keep your chest up throughout the movement.
Push your knees out in line with your toes.

stability-ball-knee-tuck.description: A plank-position knee tuck with the feet on a stability ball, rolling the ball in under the hips to load the abs dynamically.
instructions: Start in a high plank with both shins or the tops of the feet on top of a stability ball.
Hands are under the shoulders, body in a straight line.
Brace the core and pull the ball toward the chest by tucking the knees in.
Roll it back out by extending the legs fully back to the plank position.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.
tips: Hips do not pike up; keep a level trunk throughout the roll-in.
Shoulders stay over the wrists — don't let them drift forward.

stair-climber.description: A cardio machine movement that climbs a revolving staircase step after step, loading the glutes and quads continuously with no landing impact.
instructions: Step onto the bottom stair with the machine at its slowest setting and take the rails lightly for balance.
Climb one step at a time, placing the whole foot on each stair rather than just the toes.
Stand upright with your chest open and your hips under your shoulders instead of hunching over the console.
Push the step down through the heel of the front foot, letting the glute of that leg do the work.
Set the pace so you can hold your posture, and keep climbing for the desired time or number of floors.
tips: Do not lean on the rails or hook your forearms over them — supporting your weight there takes the load off the legs and the readout stops meaning anything.
Full foot on the step, heel included. Climbing on the toes shifts the whole session into the calves and burns them out early.
Take one step at a time before you try skipping steps; deliberate, upright climbing beats a fast shuffle at the bottom of the staircase.

standing-forward-fold.description: A standing stretch that lengthens the hamstrings and lower back by folding the torso over straight legs.
instructions: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and legs straight.
Hinge at your hips and fold your torso down toward the floor.
Let your hands and head hang toward your feet.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
tips: Bend your knees slightly if your hamstrings feel tight.
Ease into the stretch slowly — never bounce.

standing-side-bend.description: A standing stretch that lengthens the obliques and lats by reaching overhead and bending to one side.
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width and reach both arms overhead.
Clasp your hands and lengthen up tall.
Bend smoothly to one side in a long curve.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Switch sides and repeat.
tips: Keep both feet planted and hips steady.
Reach up and over rather than just leaning down.

step-up-to-balance.description: A single-leg step-up that finishes with a balance hold: you step onto a low platform, drive the free knee up in front of you and stand tall on the working leg before stepping back down. The quadriceps and glutes lift the body while the hips and ankle work to keep you steady.
instructions: Stand facing a low, stable step or bench and place one foot flat on top of it.
Press through the whole of the front foot and straighten that leg to lift your body onto the step.
As you rise, drive the other knee up in front of you until the thigh is about hip height.
Stand tall on the working leg and hold the knee-up position for a moment without leaning back.
Lower the free foot back to the floor under control, then step the working leg down as well.
Complete the planned repetitions on one leg, then switch to the other.
tips: Keep the whole foot on the step and push through it; pushing off the floor leg takes the work away from the front leg.
Keep the trunk upright and your hips level during the balance hold rather than tilting toward the lifted knee.
Choose a step low enough to stand up on without hopping; use a hand on a wall to start if balance is a limit.

straight-bar-cable-front-raise.description: A front raise on a low cable pulley with a straight bar attachment held in both hands. Unlike the one-armed cable front raise, both arms drive the same bar, and the cable keeps tension on the front delts through the whole range.
instructions: Attach a straight bar to a low cable pulley and stand facing away from the machine with the cable running forward past your legs.
Hold the bar with an overhand grip, hands about shoulder-width apart, arms hanging straight down in front of your thighs.
Keep the elbows almost straight and the core braced so the torso does not lean back.
Raise the bar forward in a smooth arc until it reaches shoulder height.
Lower it under control back to the thighs and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Use a light weight — swinging the bar up with the legs or leaning back takes the work off the front delts.
Stop at shoulder height; raising the bar higher shifts the load onto the traps.
Keep the wrists neutral rather than letting them bend back under the bar.

sumo-deadlift.description: A deadlift variation with a wide stance that shifts emphasis to the glutes, quads, and inner thighs.
instructions: Stand with feet wider than shoulder-width, toes pointed outward.
Grip the bar between your legs.
Brace your core and drive through your heels to stand.
Lower under control.
Repeat.
tips: Keep the bar close to your body.
Push your knees out in line with your toes.

supine-windshield-wipers.description: A lying rotation drill: with the knees bent or the legs raised, both legs swing from side to side like wipers while the shoulders stay pinned to the floor.
instructions: Lie on your back with the arms out to the sides and the knees bent over the hips.
Brace the trunk so the lower back does not lift off the floor.
Lower both legs together towards one side as far as the shoulders stay down.
Bring them back through the centre and lower to the other side.
Keep alternating for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Both shoulders stay on the floor; the range is defined by them, not by the legs.
Keep the knees together so the pelvis moves as one unit.
Straighten the legs for a much harder version once the control is there.

t-bar-row.description: A compound row performed straddling a loaded T-bar, building thickness in the lats and rhomboids.
instructions: Straddle the loaded T-bar with feet shoulder-width apart.
Hinge at the hips until your torso is around 45 degrees.
Grip the handles and keep your back flat.
Pull the bar up toward your chest by driving your elbows back.
Squeeze your shoulder blades at the top.
Lower the bar under control and repeat.
tips: Keep your hips fixed and avoid heaving the torso upright.
Maintain a soft bend in your knees to protect the lower back.
Let the weight stretch your lats fully at the bottom.

thread-the-needle-flow.description: The moving version of thread the needle: from all fours the arm threads under the body and then opens back up towards the ceiling, rotating the thoracic spine through its full range.
instructions: Start on all fours with the hands under the shoulders and the knees under the hips.
Slide one arm under the body until the shoulder approaches the mat.
Reverse the motion and open that arm up towards the ceiling, following the hand with the eyes.
Return through the centre and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Change sides and repeat.
tips: Keep the hips over the knees so the rotation stays in the upper back.
Move at an even tempo instead of throwing the arm open.
Let the head follow the hand rather than leading the movement.

torso-twists.description: A standing rotational warm-up that turns the rib cage from side to side while the pelvis stays comparatively stable, mobilising the thoracic spine and trunk.
instructions: Stand with the feet about shoulder-width apart and the knees softly bent.
Brace lightly and hold the hands together in front of the chest.
Rotate the rib cage to one side without shifting the feet.
Return through centre and rotate to the other side.
Continue alternating smoothly through a comfortable range.
tips: Turn from the upper back rather than wrenching the lower spine.
Keep the hips mostly forward and distribute the weight evenly between the feet.
Use a controlled rhythm; this is mobility work, not a ballistic swing.

tricep-kickback.description: An isolation exercise for the triceps performed in a bent-over position with a dumbbell in each hand.
instructions: Hinge forward at the hips, holding a dumbbell in each hand with the elbows bent at 90 degrees.
Extend both arms straight back, squeezing the triceps.
Hold briefly at full extension.
Lower with control.
Repeat for the planned number of reps.
tips: Keep your elbows close to your sides and finish with your arms in line with your torso.
Use light dumbbells and avoid swinging them with momentum.
Keep your back flat and your knees slightly bent to hold the hinge.

trx-bicep-curl.description: This exercise uses a suspension trainer to isolate and strengthen the biceps brachii and brachialis muscles, building upper arm strength and hypertrophy.
instructions: Adjust the suspension trainer straps to a medium length.
Stand facing the anchor point, grasp the handles with an underhand grip, and lean back until your arms are fully extended.
Keep your body straight and core engaged, pull your chest towards your hands by bending your elbows.
Squeeze your biceps at the top of the movement.
Slowly extend your arms back to the starting position, controlling the descent.
Maintain tension throughout the set.
tips: Adjust your body angle to increase or decrease difficulty; leaning further back makes it harder.
Keep your elbows high and fixed to isolate the biceps effectively.
Avoid swinging your body or using momentum; focus on a controlled contraction.
Ensure a full range of motion, from full extension to a strong peak contraction.

trx-lunge.description: A beginner-friendly unilateral lower body exercise using a suspension trainer to target the quadriceps and glutes, while also engaging the hamstrings and gluteus medius for stability.
instructions: Stand facing away from the anchor point with the suspension trainer straps behind you, hands on your hips or free for balance.
Place the top of one foot in the foot cradles and extend that leg behind you.
Brace your core and lower your body by bending the front knee, keeping your torso upright.
Descend until your front thigh is parallel to the floor or just below, maintaining tension on the suspension trainer.
Drive through your front heel to return to the starting position, extending the front leg.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch legs and repeat per side.
tips: Keep your front knee tracking over your toes, avoiding inward collapse.
Maintain a neutral spine throughout the movement, preventing excessive arching or rounding.
Control the eccentric (lowering) phase to maximize muscle engagement.
Adjust your distance from the anchor point to modify difficulty.

trx-side-plank.description: A side plank with both feet suspended in TRX cradles, intensifying the demand on the obliques.
instructions: Place both feet in the TRX foot cradles and lie on your side.
Prop up on your bottom forearm with your elbow under your shoulder.
Lift your hips so your body forms a straight line.
Stack your top foot over the bottom foot.
Hold the position while breathing steadily.
Lower and switch sides after the set.
tips: Brace your obliques before lifting your hips off the floor.
Do not let your hips drop toward the floor.
Press the forearm into the floor to keep the shoulder active.

upright-row.description: A compound pulling movement for the lateral deltoids and upper traps.
instructions: Stand holding a barbell with a shoulder-width overhand grip.
Pull the bar straight up along your body toward your chin.
Lead with your elbows, keeping them above your hands.
Lower the bar with control.
Repeat.
tips: Use a lighter weight if you feel pinching in your shoulders.
Avoid bending your wrists excessively as the bar rises.
Avoid swinging or using your legs to heave the weight up.

v-sit.description: A static core hold balancing on the sit bones with the legs and torso lifted into a V, challenging the abdominals and hip flexors.
instructions: Sit on the floor with your legs extended in front of you.
Lean back slightly and lift your legs off the floor.
Reach your arms forward so your body forms a V shape.
Balance on your sit bones with core tight.
Hold the position while breathing steadily.
Lower your legs and torso to exit.
tips: Keep your chest lifted and spine long rather than rounding the back.
Bend the knees if you cannot hold straight legs yet.

wall-ball.description: A full-body conditioning exercise that joins a front squat and a throw: holding a soft wall ball at your chest, you squat down, drive up and throw the ball to a target high on a wall, then catch it and go straight into the next squat. The legs and hips produce the power and the arms finish the throw.
instructions: Stand facing a wall about an arm's length away, feet shoulder-width apart, holding the ball at your chest with both hands.
Keep your elbows under the ball and your chest up.
Squat down until your hips are at or below knee height, keeping your heels on the floor.
Drive up hard through your legs and hips and, as you rise, throw the ball up to the target with both arms.
Catch the ball at chest height as it comes down, letting your arms absorb it.
Go straight into the next squat with the catch and repeat for the planned repetitions.
tips: Let the legs throw the ball: the push from the squat should carry it most of the way, the arms only finish the movement.
Keep your chest up and the ball close to your body in the squat so your back stays neutral.
Catch and squat in one movement; resting with the ball at the top breaks the rhythm and tires the shoulders.

warrior-one.description: A split-stance standing pose with the back foot planted at an angle, the front knee bent and the arms overhead, hips facing forward.
instructions: Step one foot back and turn it out about forty-five degrees, planting the whole sole.
Bend the front knee until it stacks over the ankle and keep the back leg straight.
Draw both hip points towards the front of the mat and lift the arms overhead.
Hold the position for the prescribed time with the ribs down and the chest lifted.
Step the feet together and repeat on the other side.
tips: Widen the stance sideways so both hips can face forward without straining the back knee.
Press the outer edge of the back foot down to keep the base stable.
Take the arms shoulder-width apart if bringing the palms together arches the lower back.

weighted-pull-up.description: A pull-up performed with extra load — most often a plate hung from a dip belt between the legs — to keep the movement in a strength rep range once bodyweight pull-ups are easy.
instructions: Attach a plate to a dip belt around your waist so the weight hangs between your legs, or hold the load between your feet.
Grip the pull-up bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width and hang at full arm extension with your legs together.
Pull your elbows down and back to drive your chest toward the bar until your chin clears it.
Lower yourself under control back to the full dead hang, keeping tension on your lats and letting the weight settle before the next rep.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Add weight only once you can do clean bodyweight pull-ups through a full range — small jumps of 2.5–5 kg are enough, since the load stacks on top of your own bodyweight.
Keep your legs together and your core braced so the hanging plate does not start swinging; a swinging weight turns the rep into a kip.
Do not cut the bottom short — return to a full dead hang each rep, and stop the set when your chin stops clearing the bar rather than grinding out partials.

wide-grip-push-ups.description: A push-up variation with a wider hand placement to emphasize the chest.
instructions: Start in a high plank with hands wider than shoulder-width.
Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Lower your chest toward the floor by bending your elbows.
Keep your core braced and glutes engaged.
Press back up until your arms are extended.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Keep your elbows at roughly 45 degrees from your torso.
Maintain a straight line from head to heels.
Lower until your chest is close to the floor.

worlds-greatest-stretch.description: A flowing mobility drill that combines a deep lunge with a trunk rotation. From a low lunge with both hands on the floor, you turn your chest toward the front leg and reach one arm to the ceiling, opening the hips, the upper back and the shoulder in one movement.
instructions: Start in a push-up position with your hands under your shoulders and your body in a straight line.
Step one foot forward, outside the same-side hand, into a deep lunge and keep the back leg straight.
Keep the hand on the back-leg side planted under your shoulder and sink your hips toward the floor.
Rotate your chest toward the front leg, lifting the arm on that side up until it points at the ceiling, and follow your hand with your eyes.
Hold the open position for a breath, then lower your hand back to the floor.
Step back to the push-up position and repeat on the other side, alternating sides for the planned repetitions.
tips: Keep the back knee off the floor and the back leg active so the stretch runs through the front of the hip.
Rotate from the upper back rather than leaning sideways; the hips stay square and low throughout.
Move slowly and breathe out as you rotate; the stretch should feel open and controlled, never forced.

zottman-curl.description: A standing dumbbell curl that lifts with a supinated grip, rotates to palms-down at the top, and lowers in pronation to combine biceps work with a forearm-heavy eccentric.
instructions: Stand with your feet about hip-width apart, arms extended at your sides, and a dumbbell in each hand with the palms facing forward.
Keep your upper arms beside your ribs and curl both dumbbells toward your shoulders without swinging the torso.
At the top, keep the elbows bent and rotate the forearms until the palms face down.
Lower the dumbbells slowly with the pronated grip until the arms are straight.
Turn the palms forward again at the bottom and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Use less weight than for a standard dumbbell curl; the palms-down lowering phase is usually the limiting part.
Rotate through the forearms while keeping the wrists straight rather than bending them around the handles.
Keep the elbows close to the ribs and avoid turning the curl into a shoulder swing.
